title: Phrasal verbs 3: out
subtitle: go out / put out, work out, find out, run out of
summary: Use phrasal verbs with out: lights going out, the many meanings of work out, and verbs such as carry out, find out, sort out and turn out.

lesson.heading: out = not burning, not shining
lesson.text: **go out** (a light, a fire), **put out** a fire / a cigarette / a light, **turn out** a light and **blow out** a candle. In all of these, out means that something stops burning or shining.

examples.text: Suddenly all the lights in the building **went out**.
I **put** the fire **out** with a fire extinguisher.
We don't need the candle. You can **blow it out**.

lesson.heading: work out - one phrasal verb, several meanings
rows: Rachel **works out** at the gym three times a week.
Good luck for the future. I hope everything **works out** well for you.
The total bill for three people is £97.35. That **works out at** £32.45 each.
345 x 76? I need a calculator. I can't **work it out** in my head.
work out / figure out = understand, find an answer
Investigators are trying to **work out** what caused the accident. or ... trying to **figure out** what caused ...
lesson.note: *A:* Why did James leave the company? *B:* Things didn't **work out**. (= things didn't work out well)

lesson.heading: carry out, find out, give out
lesson.text: **carry out** an order / an experiment / a survey / an investigation / a plan etc. **find out** that / what / when ... or **find out about** ... = get information about. **give out** or **hand out** things = give one to each person.

examples.text: Soldiers are expected to **carry out** orders.
An investigation into the accident will be **carried out**.
The police never **found out** who committed the crime.
I checked a few websites to **find out about** hotels in the town.
At the end of the lecture, the speaker **gave out** information sheets to the audience.

lesson.heading: point out, run out of, sort out
lesson.text: **point something out** (to somebody) = draw attention to it. **run out of** something = use all of it so that there is none left. **sort something out** = find a solution to it, put it in order.

examples.text: As we drove through the city, the tour guide **pointed out** all the sights.
I didn't realise I'd made a mistake until somebody **pointed it out** to me.
We **ran out of** petrol on the motorway.
There are a few problems we need to **sort out**.
All these papers are mixed up. I'll have to **sort them out**.

lesson.heading: turn out, try out
lesson.text: **turn out to be** ... / **turn out** good / nice etc. / **turn out that** ... = it became clear in the end. **try out** a machine, a system, a new idea etc. = test it to see if it is OK.

examples.text: Nobody believed Paul at first, but he **turned out to be** right.
The weather wasn't so good in the morning, but it **turned out** nice later.
I thought they knew each other, but it **turned out that** they'd never met.
The company is **trying out** some new software at the moment.

lesson.text: **run out of** always keeps its **of** before the thing that is finished: we ran out of petrol / time / money - not ~~ran out petrol~~.

exercises.prompt: Which words go together? Match each verb + out with the thing it is used with.
There was a power cut and all the lights ___.
exercises.explanation: go out = stop shining (lights) or stop burning (a fire).

exercises.prompt: Steve is very fit. He does a lot of sport and ___ regularly.
We didn't manage to discuss everything at the meeting. We ___ of time.
exercises.explanation: run out of something = use all of it so that there is none left.

exercises.prompt: The road will be closed for two days while building work is ___.
exercises.explanation: carry out work / a plan / an investigation = do it.

exercises.prompt: What does work out mean in each sentence?

items.text: Rachel works out at the gym three times a week.
I hope everything works out well for you.
I need a calculator. I can't work it out in my head.
Things didn't work out, so James left the company.
Investigators are trying to work out what caused the accident.
Sally and Kim are working out at the gym.
The bill works out at £32.45 each.

exercises.prompt: We thought she was American at first, but she ___ to be Swedish.
exercises.explanation: turn out to be = it became clear in the end that ...

exercises.statement: The new drug will be tried out on a small group of patients.
exercises.explanation: Correct. try out = test something to see if it is OK.

exercises.statement: We ran out petrol on the motorway and had to walk to the nearest garage.
exercises.explanation: We ran out of petrol on the motorway. run out OF something.

exercises.prompt: They got married a few years ago, but it didn't ___ and they separated.
exercises.explanation: work out = develop or progress well. Things didn't work out = things didn't go well.

exercises.prompt: 'How much money do I owe you exactly?' Say that you need a moment to calculate it.
exercises.answer: Just a moment. I'll have to work it out.
exercises.explanation: work it out = calculate it; the pronoun goes in the middle.

exercises.prompt: 'You've written the wrong date on this form.' 'Oh, so I have. Thanks for ___.'
exercises.explanation: point something out = draw attention to it. After thanks for we use -ing.
